a meningioma in a boxer bitch metastasized to the lungs and that immunohistochemically the tumor cells were not positive with antibodies to GFAPP, S-100, NSE, cytokeratin and desmin, but positive with vimentin and factor VIII related antigen.

a) a malignant meningioma was diagnosed in a dog with pulmonary metastases; b) the tumor had the histologic appearance of a meningotheliomatosis; c) the tumor cells showed a positive reaction with the antibody to vimentin and a negative reaction with antibodies to all other antigens investigated; d) the results of the immunohistochemical investigation were identical in seven additional canine meningiomas.
a ten-year-old boxer dog had seizures and strabismus, and at necropsy had a malignant meningioma with metastases to the lung.

a rare case of a dog with meningioma with metastases to the lung.

meningiomas of dogs, as well as of other species, are not of mesodermal origin, as has often been assumed.

the immunohistochemical examination with antibodies to GFPA, S-100 and vimentin is not helpful for the diagnosis of canine meningiomas.

the immunohistochemical examination with antibodies to GF AP, S-100, NSE, cytokeratin and vimentin is not helpful to differentiate between benign and malignant meningiomas, whereas the immunohistochemistry for factor VIII related antigen may be useful for the diagnosis of a meningiomas with a tendency to metastasize.

The main takeaway from our work is that
meningioma is a rare disease in dogs, and that it should be considered in the differential diagnosis of intracranial masses.
meningioma can metastasize to lungs and that the prognosis for dogs diagnosed with this condition is poor.
the prognosis for dogs with meningiomas is poor and that the prognosis is even worse for dogs with meningotheliomatosis.
